proof_summary: For \(n=550172=4\cdot343\cdot401\), the period \(29400\) reduces the search to finitely many exponent classes; a modular computation shows that residue \(13573\) is not attained for any \(k\le16{,}331{,}503\), while a 196-entry table and the Chinese remainder theorem show that every residue is attained by \(k\le82{,}496{,}875\), so the least covering index is at least \(16{,}331{,}504\). A finite sieve and composite-count bound show that at least \(550172\) primes lie below \(8{,}165{,}754\), hence \(2(p_{550172}-1)\le16{,}331{,}504\), contradicting the proposed strict inequality.
